The struct returns to being an implementation detail. Under that target the field-parity question dissolves: single-platform fields keep platform scope through the CFG_FIELD_LIST_PLATFORM mechanism that already exists, so merging the struct does not force merging the field set and NO struct has to grow. W3 builds the keyed store; it does not litigate 16 fields.

Measured: 266 preferences.put/get calls in src/esp32/esp32_flash.cpp; nRF52's compat merge at src/nrf52/nrf52_flash.cpp:113-140 with MESHCOM_COMPAT_MARKER 0x57 (WisBlock-API.h:412). spec: One schema (config_json.cpp's X() table) drives BOTH the JSON surface and persistence, on BOTH platforms, with records addressed by key. nRF52: run the OPT-03-approved compat migration ONCE -- read the old blob through s_meshcomcompat_settings, write the keyed store -- then retire the compat struct permanently, so no future generation adds another frozen byte-layout twin. ESP32 is NOT already correct: its persistence is key-addressed (so a layout change fails soft) but the key list is maintained by hand and separately from X(), so a field added to the struct and to X() but forgotten in esp32_flash.cpp silently never persists. Both platforms today maintain the same field mapping twice by hand; the target is that neither does.

pair: C4 gateway TX pass -- per-loop-pass UDP-out drain trigger
esp32_behaviour: gatewayService_esp32() calls getMeshComUDP() then unconditionally sendMeshComUDP() on every pass where bGATEWAY && node_hasIPaddress, regardless of whether a packet was received this pass (src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20-22).
nrf52_behaviour: gatewayService_nrf52() only calls sendUDP() inside the branch where neth.getUDP()==1 (i.e. NO packet was received this pass); when a packet WAS received, the else branch sets bUDPReceived=true and sendUDP() is skipped entirely for that pass (src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:32-38).
evidence: src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20-22 vs. src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:22-45. No twin test exists for gatewayService_*() (not one of the six required suites; C4 is a carve-out, not yet characterized by a U-suite) -- source-sourced.
recommendation: DECIDED 2026-09-12 both-valid, STAYS SPLIT -- the audit's 'ESP32 looks correct' is REJECTED. On RAK4631 the W5100S and the SX1262 share the SPI bus. gatewayService_nrf52() wraps the Ethernet access in bSPI_ETH_Active (gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:30,43), which tells the LoRa side the bus is taken (lora_functions.cpp:538,2403-2410) and DEFERS radio re-arm until release (bPendingRadioRx -> startRadioReceive()). Draining TX on every RX pass would lengthen that window, and a radio that is late back into receive MISSES LoRa frames. ESP32 has no such cost, so its unconditional drain is correct FOR ESP32 and not a template for nRF52. The trade is real in both directions -- starve the uplink, or delay the radio -- and nRF52 picks the radio, which is the right priority for a mesh node. RESIDUAL RISK, accepted knowingly: under sustained inbound traffic the nRF52 TX ring drains only on passes with no RX. REVISIT IF observed -- the symptom would be outbound UDP latency or ring overflow on RAK-90 under load, not anything visible at idle. pair: preconditions before the UDP-out drain runs at all

(1) PRECONDITIONS, nRF52: give sendUDP() its own equivalents of ESP32's three early returns (neth.hasIPaddress, unresolved destination address, and the AP-mode analogue if one exists) so it does not enter the drain on a known-bad link. pair: encodeAPRS()/decodeAPRS() epilogue SUB-byte round trip (SHARED code -- src/aprs_functions.cpp is one file linked into both firmware images; no ESP32-vs-nRF52 split for this row) [OPT-D15]
esp32_behaviour: Same as nRF52 -- shared implementation. Encoder substitutes SUB=0x00 with 0x23 ('#') but writes SUB=0x7E VERBATIM (src/aprs_functions.cpp:1356-1359), producing two consecutive 0x7E bytes on the wire when a node's sub-version is literally 0x7E ('~').
nrf52_behaviour: Same as ESP32 -- shared implementation. Decoder reads the first 0x7E of that pair back as '#' (src/aprs_functions.cpp:469-473) and separately consumes the second 0x7E as the frame terminator: a node whose sub-version is 0x7E silently becomes '#' after one hop, on any receiver, regardless of platform.
evidence: docs/BACKLOG.md OPT-D15 (~line 4612); test/test_aprs_epilogue/test_aprs_epilogue.cpp:298-316 (test_epilogue_sub_0x7e_collision, 4/4 mutations caught per the backlog entry)
recommendation: DECIDED 2026-09-12 both-valid -- NO CODE CHANGE, EVER, by choice. 0x7E is declared an ILLEGAL sub-version value and documented as reserved; the constraint is written down instead of engineered around. FRAMING CORRECTED: this is NOT cross-platform drift. src/aprs_functions.cpp is one shared file linked into both images, so both platforms carry the behaviour identically and there is no 'side' to be correct. It is in the matrix because U7 found it, not because it is drift. EXPOSURE, which is what decided it: SOURCE_VERSION_SUB is "t" (src/configuration_global.h:2) and the sub-version is a single version letter incremented by a human. No shipped firmware has used 0x7E ('~') and nothing would choose it. So the fix would change an encoder every node in the network already agrees on -- a real fleet-coordination window -- to protect a value nobody will pick. OWED (documentation, not code): record in docs/architecture/11-wire-format.md that the epilogue SUB byte reserves 0x00 (already substituted with 0x23 by the encoder, aprs_functions.cpp:1356) and 0x7E (the frame terminator; written verbatim by the encoder and read back as '#' by the decoder at :469-473, hence lossy). test/test_aprs_epilogue keeps the behaviour pinned -- its role changes from 'pinning a bug' to 'showing why the value is reserved'. Supersedes OPT-D15's 'owed a decision' status in BACKLOG.md; update that row. REVIEW 2026-09-12: class corrected to cosmetic (shared code, like DR-28/29). Confirmed enforceable: no runtime path sets the SUB byte, and the decoder's 0x7E->'#' (aprs_functions.cpp:470-473) is the guard that holds across relays; the wire-format note must record BOTH guards. The '4/4 mutations caught' figure has no artefact in the tree.
